missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend high-dose vitamin C until stone history/type, kidney function and total intake from all products are clarified.
safety_exclusions: Do not assume every kidney-stone type has the same relationship to vitamin C.
Do not infer vitamin C deficiency from stone history.
Do not recommend high-dose vitamin C as a general wellness measure.
professional_escalation_conditions: Recurrent calcium oxalate stones, chronic kidney disease, hyperoxaluria or prior oxalate nephropathy.
population_and_context: People with a history of kidney stones considering vitamin C supplements; high supplemental vitamin C intake may increase urinary oxalate in some contexts.
dose_constraints: No dose from this rule. Reconcile total vitamin C intake and obtain clinician/urology guidance for recurrent stone disease.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Vitamin C fact sheet describes potential oxalate-related concerns at high supplemental intakes; individual stone risk requires clinical assessment.
